review_candidates.title: Verpleegkundige - Prinsenhof - West Vlaanderen
review_candidates.description: We zoeken een enthousiaste Verpleegkundige met een hart voor ouderen . Je hebt een erkend diploma Verpleegkunde; Je hebt een geldig visum van de FOD Volksgezondheid; Je spreekt vlot Nederlands; Je kunt overweg met zorgsoftware – of je hebt hier interesse in. Heb je na het lezen van deze tekst zin om meer te weten? Misschien bezit je daarnaast over persoonlijke superpowers die het verschil kunnen maken? Laat dan zeker van je horen. Emotionele momenten, veel verantwoordelijkheid, ... werken als Verpleegkundige is pittig – dat moeten we jou niet vertellen. Maar jouw werk is ook waardevol en bijzonder belangrijk. Daarom doen we ons best om jou te ondersteunen, zodat jij alles kunt geven voor de bewoners en dicht bij jezelf kan blijven. Bij ons blijft je werk boeiend en gevarieerd, en je staat er nooit alleen voor. Je komt terecht in een gezellig team waar we hard werken maar ook graag eens lachen. Jij verdient meer dan alleen een professionele werkplek. Een ruime ontspanningsruimte, een groene omgeving, een plek waar je je snel goed zal voelen! From UHF CB radios trusted by four-wheel drivers, transport operators and emergency services, to emergency beacons that play a critical role in search and rescue operations, our products are designed, engineered and manufactured right here in Australia. For more than 65 years, GME has built a reputation for creating reliable communication and safety technology that performs in the harshest conditions. We're proudly Australian-owned and one of the few companies in our industry with end-to-end capabilities spanning research, design, engineering, testing and manufacturing. We're now looking for a Senior RF Design Engineer to join our Engineering team and help shape the next generation of communication and safety products used across Australia and beyond. Why this role is different This isn't a role where you'll be designing components that disappear into someone else's product. At GME, you'll work on complete RF design systems that make it into the hands of customers and are relied upon in real-world, mission-critical situations. You'll have the opportunity to: Design and develop RF solutions for market-leading communication and emergency beacon products Influence technical direction and product architecture Work closely with electronics, mechanical, firmware and manufacturing teams Take products from concept through to production Validate designs using dedicated RF test and development facilities Contribute to products that have a genuine impact on safety and rescue outcomes If you enjoy solving challenging RF problems and want to see your designs make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you. What you'll be doing As a Senior RF Design Engineer, you'll be responsible for the design, development and optimisation of RF circuits and systems for new and existing GME products. You'll: Design RF circuits including amplifiers, filters, mixers and oscillators Develop, simulate, analyse and optimise RF system performance Prototype, test and validate RF designs using industry-standard test equipment Lead RF design activities across the product development lifecycle Investigate complex technical issues and implement robust engineering solutions Support schematic capture, component selection and PCB design reviews Ensure designs meet regulatory, performance and manufacturing requirements Work closely with manufacturing teams to transition products successfully into production Collaborate with project managers and cross-functional engineering teams to deliver projects on time and to specification Contribute to technical documentation, design reviews and continuous improvement initiatives What we're looking for We're interested in engineers who are passionate about RF design and enjoy creating products that solve real-world problems. You'll bring: Essential Degree qualification in Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering or a related discipline Extensive experience designing and developing RF circuits and systems Strong knowledge of RF amplifiers, filters, oscillators, mixers and associated design principles Experience with RF simulation and design tools such as ADS, LTspice and Altium Hands-on experience with PCB design, prototyping, bring-up and validation Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis skills Experience using RF test equipment including spectrum analysers, signal generators, oscilloscopes and power meters Excellent communication skills and the ability to work across multidisciplinary engineering teams Eligibility to obtain and maintain an Australian Government NV1 Security Clearance Highly regarded Experience developing communication or radio-based products Knowledge of analogue, digital and mixed-signal circuit design Experience with radio modulation techniques including AM, FM and digital radio technologies Experience working within ISO9001, AS9100 or similar quality environments Experience supporting products from concept through manufacturing and production release Join us At GME, engineering sits at the heart of what we do. If you're an experienced RF Engineer looking for an opportunity to solve meaningful technical challenges, build products used in the real world, and be part of a team that's proud of the impact it makes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and help engineer the technology Australians rely on when communication matters most.

review_candidates.title: Senior Manager, Center of Excellence
review_candidates.description: Senior Manager, Center of Excellence Singapore | Full Time | Permanent About DayOne DayOne builds and operates hyperscale data centers across nine markets in APAC and Europe. We raised US$4.5B in Series C funding and are scaling fast across Southeast Asia. In Singapore, our home market and regional headquarters, we hold one of only four permits under Singapore's Pilot DC-CFA and are pioneering Solid Oxide Fuel Cell technology at Jurong East as a proof of concept for hydrogen-based power generation. This is where DayOne's regional strategy is shaped and where what comes next gets built first — and as the project delivery portfolio grows across markets, the internal infrastructure governing how projects are delivered has to scale with it. About the Role You'll establish and run DayOne's Center of Excellence for project delivery — designing the standards, frameworks, and processes that govern how data center projects are delivered across the SEA region. This is a process-builder and standards-owner role. You will not be executing project. You will be building the system that makes every project better. This role suits someone who thinks in systems, writes with precision, and has spent meaningful time in data center, construction, or mission-critical infrastructure environments. This role requires data center, construction, or mission-critical infrastructure experience. Candidates from SaaS, IT services, banking, or financial services will not be considered. Policy and Process Standardization Design and own standardized project delivery processes, documentation protocols, and internal control frameworks across the SEA portfolio. Define clear roles, responsibilities, and demarcation across functions and markets. Embed compliance and risk mitigation into all process design from the outset — not as a retrofit. Project Delivery Oversight Develop and maintain delivery assessment frameworks for individual and team performance management across the portfolio. Collaborate with Account Delivery Managers to tailor delivery approaches to client and project-specific requirements. Conduct regular on-site inspections across active data center projects in Southeast Asia. Competency and Team Development Lead competency assessments in partnership with HR to identify capability gaps across delivery teams. Design and implement targeted training programs and incentive mechanisms to strengthen team capability across markets. Reporting and Analytics Consolidate project data across the delivery portfolio and maintain a single, accurate view of delivery performance for senior leadership. Build and maintain dashboards for internal management and senior leadership reporting across the SEA portfolio. Requirements Technical Skills 5 or more years of experience in PMO, project management, or delivery management, with at least 3 years in data center, construction, or mission-critical infrastructure. Demonstrated experience designing business processes and policy documentation from the ground up in a multi-market environment. Strong command of project management methodologies and tools. Fluent in English and Chinese — required for effective cross-market stakeholder engagement across DayOne's SEA operations. Comfortable with regular travel to Johor and across Southeast Asia. Soft Skills Builds process frameworks that people in the field use Influences cross-functional stakeholders across markets without direct authority, using credibility and precision rather than hierarchy. Identifies delivery gaps and systemic risks across the portfolio and escalates with a proposed solution, not just an observation. Nice to Have PMP, ITIL, or equivalent project management certification. Direct data center construction or operations background. Proficiency with AI productivity tools in a professional setting. Why DayOne? This is a Singapore-based role with regional reach and direct visibility to senior leadership. You'll build a function from the ground up — owning the standards and frameworks that govern how DayOne delivers across Southeast Asia. The scope is real, the mandate is clear, and the impact is visible across every project the region runs. If you build clarity where there is none and want your work to shape how an entire region operates, the platform here is the right size and the timing is right.

review_candidates.title: Senior Manager Investigations
review_candidates.description: Senior Manager, Investigations GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist , NPR , TED , and The Washington Post . We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.  Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! About this role GiveDirectly is looking for an experienced investigator who can establish a function, not just run cases. Concerns and allegations reach us from every program and every country we work in. Each one needs to be triaged and assessed objectively, and to end in appropriate findings and recommendations. You will manage the newly created Central Intake and Investigations Hub. It is a standalone, independent function that works across the whole organisation. The Hub investigates a range of investigations itself, and supports colleagues elsewhere who handle the rest. You will lead the team and take the most complex investigations yourself. The bigger initial task is to establish the Hub across the organisation. How it works has been designed and agreed. What it does not yet have is standing. People need to know it exists, bring things to it early, and trust what it concludes. This matters now because GiveDirectly is growing fast. Delivery volume and headcount are both rising, and the way staff concerns are handled needs to grow with them. Reports to: Director of Safeguarding and Investigations Manages: Future roles including a Program Manager, Investigations and Program Manager, Intake and Reporting to be recruited once the Senior Manager role has been filled.  Level: Senior Manager  Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time. Travel: Occasional. Team meetings and co-locations, plus travel to a country of operation where an investigation requires it. This is not frequent, but it is not predictable either. What you'll do Establish a Central Intake and Investigations Hub across the organisation: Take an agreed design and make it something people use. Build the relationships with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, HR Managers and Country Directors to ensure concerns are managed effectively. Refine how intake, triage and allocation work in practice as you learn what holds up. Lead the most complex investigations yourself. Establish the facts, produce the findings report and make recommendations. Set the investigation standard and hold other people to it: Define what a good investigation looks like at GiveDirectly. Provide oversight and support where Internal Audit or Safeguarding lead a staff related matter, and quality assure what comes out of it. Decide what training the organisation needs and set its direction. Own the record and what it tells the organisation: Create and hold the system of record for staff matters. Make sure findings and documentation are captured centrally, whoever led the case. Run regular reporting and calibration with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, Country Directors and ExCo. Sign off on relevant internal and external reporting.  Make the function work at scale through the responsible use of technology and data: Shape the design of the case management system and its controls, so that staff investigation records sit only where they should. Find the practical places where automation and AI reduce manual work in triage, documentation and reporting. Build the hub so that growth in concern volume does not simply mean a bigger team. Set up and lead the team: Recruit for, manage and develop a Program Manager, Investigations and the Program Manager, Intake and Reporting. Set their priorities, review their work and build their capability. What success looks like in 12 to 18 months Concerns reach the hub as a matter of course, from every country and function. People come to the hub early and while a matter is still manageable, because they have found it useful rather than because they were told to. Investigations are handled consistently, whoever leads them, and findings reports hold up when they are challenged. The hub is understood across the organisation as an independent central resource. Internal and External reporting tells its audience something they did not already know about patterns, themes and where risk is concentrating. The People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership treat the hub as a resource they rely on rather than a process they comply with. Additional hires for the hub are capable, developing, and the function runs day to day without you in the room. Why this role You build it. This is a new function with a mandate and a set of agreed boundaries. How it actually works is largely what you make it. Genuine independence. The hub is designed to be objective and to handle complex matters. Breadth. You will work across every function and every country GiveDirectly operates in. It matters. Getting this right protects staff and recipients, and protects the trust that lets GiveDirectly move a great deal of money to people who need it. What we are looking for: How you work matters as much as your investigation skills. Trusted by the people you also hold to account. You can tell someone that the handling of a matter was wrong, and still have a strong working relationship with them the following week. People Managers, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership should want to call you early rather than after things have gone wrong. You motivate and influence people who don't report to you. The Hub has no direct line management over Internal Audit, Safeguarding, the People team or country leadership, and it needs all of them to do the work well. You build the relationships and shape best practice. Impartial, and visibly so. People may try to influence you. You will be told the answer before you have found it. You hold to process and evidence without turning it into a fight, and you record what you could not establish as carefully as what you could. You build what isn't there yet. This function is being shaped by you. You are comfortable where the priorities are clear, but the road to them is not. You would rather design a solution rather than wait to be handed one. You work alongside people. Some of the investigative work is done by other teams, and your expertise is what lifts its quality. You get into the detail with colleagues, you are clear about what good looks like and what still needs doing, and you see it through with them. Steady with difficult material. You work with content of abuse and misconduct without losing sight of the people involved, and without carrying it in ways that wear you down. On experience, we are looking for: Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity.  5-7 years of experience leading workplace (misconduct) investigations , including matters involving senior staff and allegations of sexual misconduct. You have run these end to end, from terms of reference to findings report. Experience in setting investigation standards and quality assuring other people's work , not only conducting investigations yourself. A working understanding of employee relations and of where an investigation ends and an employment decision begins. You have worked alongside other teams without blurring the lines of responsibility. Experience across multiple countries and legal contexts , including where local law shapes how we may investigate and how staff must be treated. Trauma-informed and survivor-centred practice in how you plan interviews, handle disclosures and support the people involved. Has made technology work for investigative teams. You have set up or improved investigative system, built reporting from case data, or introduced tools that changed how a team worked. You have used AI in professional work and can say where it helped, where it did not, and how you handled confidentiality. Language Requirement: Professional fluency in English, plus professional working proficiency in one of French, Swahili or Portuguese. Investigative interviews are often confidential and conducted in these languages. Why work at GiveDirectly? At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including: A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement  A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow A competitive salary, including bonus A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country) Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!) Read more about our ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts here and about our decision to move our central support teams to remote first here .

review_candidates.description: About Us SPH Media’s mission is to be the trusted source of news and lifestyle content in Singapore and Asia. One of our core purposes is to produce credible, balanced, and objective news and analysis, always with a view to uphold the public good and fostering an informed, engaged citizenry. We welcome talented individuals to join us and grow a career in a vibrant and collaborative environment built around a culture of respect and inclusivity. As an employer, we are committed to rewarding our people fairly and developing them in their careers. About the Role As a Senior Cloud Platform Engineer, you will design, build, and maintain the scalable infrastructure that powers our services. You are a specialist in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation, ensuring our cloud ecosystems are secure, cost-effective, and highly resilient. Our Platform Engineering Culture Customer Obsession: We don't build tech for tech's sake; we build to empower our developers and deliver value to our end users. Psychological Safety: We foster an environment where everyone feels safe to voice concerns and challenge the status quo. We embrace fail-safe engineering and prioritize learning from failures through a strictly blameless culture. Practical Integrity: We "do the next right thing" by prioritizing long-term platform health over quick fixes, while remaining pragmatic about delivery timelines. Constructive Transparency: We value honest feedback and open communication as the primary drivers of business success and operational reliability. Key Responsibilities Infrastructure as Code: Architect and manage cloud environments using Terraform and Python to ensure repeatable and version-controlled deployments. Workload Portability: Leverage Kubernetes (K8s) and Helm charts to build an open, stable application platform that ensures consistent performance and operational flexibility across different environments. CI/CD Leadership: Maintain and optimize automated workflows via GitHub to ensure high-velocity engineering. Operational Excellence: Provide expert-level management of AWS infrastructure while ensuring technical standards are compatible with diverse architectural requirements. Security & FinOps: Implement "Security by Design" principles and proactively optimize cloud spend to balance performance with cost-efficiency. Availability & Reliability: Participate in a shared on-call rotation to support critical production infrastructure, ensuring high uptime and rapid incident response. Required Qualifications Core Tools: Minimum 3+ years of hands-on experience with Terraform, GitHub, and Python. Cloud Platforms: Extensive experience with AWS (Required); a strong understanding of building flexible, adaptable infrastructure patterns. Containerization: Advanced knowledge of Kubernetes (K8s) focusing on platform stability and standardized deployment strategies. Agile Mindset: Deep familiarity with Agile and Scrum methodologies. Incident Management: Experience using Jira Service Management (JSM) for tracking incidents and maintaining post-mortem documentation. Experience: 5+ years total in a DevOps, SRE, or Platform Engineering role.

SAR Paramedics will work closely with members of the Aero-Medical Evacuation (AME) team to provide emergency treatment and coordinate medical evacuations. This position requires a high level of physical fitness and the ability to work in challenging conditions, including hot and humid environments, adverse weather, varied terrain, and different altitudes. Strong experience as an acute/emergency care paramedic, including advanced emergency response in a variety of settings (rural, urban, and industrial). Knowledge of and experience in the aviation industry, particularly aero-medical evacuation. Previous Aero-Medical Evacuation (AME), Technical Rescue, and/or Search & Rescue (SAR) experience. Ability to provide emergency response independently or as part of an Emergency Response Team (ERT), Search & Rescue (SAR) team, or Aero-Medical Evacuation (AME) team. Vehicle and Aircraft Rescue Extrication Training. Helicopter Underwater Escape Training (HUET). BOSIET Strong written and verbal English communication skills. Travel / Rotation Requirements Permanent positions: 5 weeks on / 5 weeks off rotation. Locum assignments: Rotation lengths vary depending on operational requirements. Key Responsibilities Perform advanced rescue operations across a range of environments. Provide emergency medical care in high-risk and remote settings. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams during rescue missions. Maintain operational readiness and adhere to safety protocols. Participate in ongoing training, simulations, and competency assessments. Core Rescue Disciplines The role may involve expertise in one or more of the following areas: High-angle (rope) rescue Motor vehicle extrication Confined space rescue Structural collapse rescue Trench rescue Aquatic and swift water rescue Aviation rescue What We're Looking For We are seeking highly capable and adaptable paramedics who thrive in demanding environments and are passionate about emergency response, technical rescue, and delivering exceptional patient care in remote and industrial settings. Successful candidates will demonstrate strong clinical judgment, technical rescue capability, teamwork, resilience, and a commitment to safety excellence. Location: Papua New Guinea Employment Type: Permanent and Locum Opportunities Available Roster: Permanent positions operate on a 5 weeks on / 5 weeks off rotation, while locum assignments vary based on operational requirements.
